Qix npm account shipped wallet drainers

Target: qix-npm-account
Date: 2025-09-08
Actor: Third Party (group)
Target Kind: library
Language: JavaScript
Cause: social_engineering
Motive: financial_gain
Transitive: false
Impact: credential_theft, financial_exploitation, self_propagation
User Impact: 0
Phase: distribution
Campaigns: Qix phishing shipped wallet drainers

Synopsis

Attackers phished Qix through npmjs.help and published malicious releases across widely used npm packages. Browser bundles could redirect crypto transactions.

Story

The Qix compromise began with a convincing npm support phish. The fake `npmjs.help` flow captured maintainer access from Josh Junon, known as Qix, and gave the attacker publishing rights to foundational JavaScript packages.

The first wave landed on September 8, 2025. Packages such as `debug`, `chalk`, `ansi-regex`, `strip-ansi`, `wrap-ansi`, and related terminal and color utilities received malicious versions. Their aggregate weekly download count was enormous, but downloads are exposure, not confirmed victims.

The payload was built for browsers. It hooked wallet and network APIs, watched for Ethereum, Bitcoin, Solana, Tron, Litecoin, and related transaction material, and replaced destination addresses or approvals with attacker-controlled values. Server-side installs were still poisoned artifacts, but the theft path needed bundled client-side execution.

Cleanup required removing the bad npm versions, purging registry caches, deleting `node_modules`, and rebuilding deployed browser bundles from clean packages. Follow-on compromised packages are grouped in the Qix campaign; this record carries the packages controlled by the Qix npm account.
